trace.topic: Dear SaaStr: Should I Use an AI SDR Before I Have a Working Human SDR motion?
trace.goal: Advise founders on whether AI SDRs can substitute for an unproven outbound motion.
expected_facts: The answer should argue that AI cannot fix a broken outbound motion by itself.
It should explain that founders still need a working message, ICP, and qualification logic.
It should allow that AI can accelerate a working system but rarely invent one from nothing.
rubric_must_haves: Explains what parts of the motion must already work.
Uses practical examples or failure modes.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should say that founders should not expect an AI SDR to invent a working go-to-market motion. If the ICP, messaging, and follow-up logic are still broken, automating them only scales the noise. AI SDRs work best when there is already a credible human playbook to copy and improve.

So there's a lot of controversy today around this topic on whether you should use an AI SDR before you have a working human SDR process.
And my basic view is if your team can't get it done, why would you trust them with something more complicated? But let me just share some learnings here and then we'll see what our speakers say.
First off, everyone uses AIs now. So many folks think they're using one, but so many aren't actually using any sort of AI tool.
We've talked about this before, but I was at a board meeting recently where two reps walked in and said "Oh yeah, we're running Claude."
I'm like, well, no, you're not because it takes work to train an agent. And when we looked at their data, we saw nothing had been trained yet. It was blank.
But there's another thing too. If your humans can't close anything, it doesn't matter how good the AI is. There are so many reasons to try AI SDRs.
First off, they don't quit.

Dear SaaStr: Should I Use an AI SDR Before You Have a Working Human SDR Motion?
Yes.
In fact, you probably need to use one before you hire your first true sales rep if possible — or at least very early on.  At least experiment with using them earlier than most founders think they can afford to. This was my experience when I sold EchoSign / Adobe Sign. We had no sales team until $100k MRR.
Our CEO Sam Blond joined later as VP Sales at $700k MRR. But we started experimenting with outbound email marketing (a lot) once our leads were high quality enough:
We ran campaigns ourselves where every day we'd send out emails. Every single day, every hour of the day, we'd send out emails. And then we brought in two part-time contractors just doing cold calling and emailing. They worked out really well. Then we hired full-time reps. Those contractors did better than any human SDRs ever did for us. 95% of human SDRs don't even know their products anyway. They're too lazy. It takes too long to learn anything. So this contractor knew everything. He could tell his story, tell how EchoSign was used, how many Fortune 500 companies already used it. All those things. He got meetings.
Then we went to the next level. We added a few more people to the team. Now we've gone all-in with AI agents. But here's what I would say to folks now: if you want to get ahead today, I think everyone needs to start running these experiments immediately. Don't wait until you go live. If you're going to run outbound, start sending outbound yourself. Run some campaigns. Try different approaches. That will actually train the agent so when you put it into production, it works. I'm running five AI agents myself right now. Five! And the ones that work best are the ones that had me involved in training them personally. The ones that didn't work were the ones I wasn't trained properly by someone.

The Single Best Use Case to Start With: The Leads Your Team Is Ignoring
This is the insight that changed how we think about AI SDRs entirely. Your human SDRs are force-ranking in their heads every single day. They’re chasing the big deals, the warm inbound, the accounts that feel like they could close this quarter. The leads they consider “not worth it” — return event attendees, old website visitors, ghosted CRM contacts — those get nothing. Not bad follow-up. Nothing. That’s where AI SDRs absolutely shine. When we deployed AI on the leads our human team refused to work — people who had engaged with SaaStr but never got follow-up — we got a
72% open rate
on Agentforce and generated
15% of our London event revenue
from a segment that would have produced zero without AI. Not 15% incremental lift. 15% of total revenue from leads that were producing $0. So before you start thinking about AI SDRs as a way to scale your best motion, ask yourself: what’s the motion your team isn’t running at all? Start there.
